problems.memo_sentence: "For the QAMC-based benchmark, the authors recall that amplitude-estimation-based Monte Carlo achieves a quadratic improvement in the number of queries needed for a given mean squared error compared to classical Monte Carlo."
problems.source_evidence: "Since this method can be computationally demanding for certain types of integrals, in recent years the advantages offered by quantum computing have been exploited to develop the QAMC method [26], which achieves a quadratic improvement, in terms of the mean squared error, in the number of queries required compared to its classical counterpart."
problems.explanation: The quadratic speedup is presented in the paper as a property of QAMC cited from reference [26], not as a result established by this paper itself. The memo attributes the claim to the authors of this paper rather than to the cited prior work.

problems.memo_sentence: "The authors formulate pricing either via Fourier series of the probability density function (PDF) or of the cumulative distribution function (CDF), so that the integral becomes a sum over products of Fourier coefficients associated with the distribution and the payoff."
problems.source_evidence: "By substituting equation (6) into equation (5), we obtain ... It should be noted that Ck and Dk are the coefficients of the trigonometric Fourier series of h(T, y). Thus, the integral of the product of two real functions, f(y|x) and h(T, y) has been transformed into the sum of the product of the respective coefficients of their trigonometric Fourier series." and for the CDF route: "It should be remarked that, in contrast with the previous method, the quantities defined in (10) do not correspond to the Fourier coefficients of the series that approximates h(T, y), because the integration domain does not match with the one of the basis functions."
problems.explanation: The memo collapses the two methods into a single statement that pricing becomes a sum over Fourier coefficients. The paper explicitly warns that in the CDF method the quantities in (10) are not Fourier coefficients of the payoff series, so the simplification is not generally true.

problems.memo_sentence: "The authors formulate pricing either via Fourier series of the probability density function (PDF) or of the cumulative distribution function (CDF), so that the integral becomes a sum over products of Fourier coefficients associated with the distribution and the payoff."
problems.source_evidence: "In finance, it is common to work in practice with PDFs whose tails tend to vanish, so it can be assumed that there exists an interval [a, b] ⊂ R such that the integral in (4) can be approximated without significant loss of accuracy" and "Therefore, working directly with the PDF can be numerically unstable or ill-posed."
problems.explanation: The memo omits the paper's explicit limitation that the PDF approach relies on truncating the domain to a finite interval and that direct PDF handling can be numerically unstable or ill-posed. This limitation is central to why the CDF method is introduced.

problems.memo_sentence: "The work proposes two hybrid classical–quantum methods based on parametrized quantum circuits (PQCs) acting as trainable function approximators whose output functions admit a Fourier series representation with a frequency spectrum determined by the encoding Hamiltonians."
problems.source_evidence: "Several results show that incorporating this information can significantly improve a model’s training performance, as it forces the function estimates to converge point-wise rather than on average." and "Another significant aspect that has to be taken into account is that the model to obtain the statistical functions is going to be trained in [−2π, 2π] with data rescaled to [−π, π], rather than trained directly in [−π, π]. This ensures that the resulting Fourier series is smoother and does not exhibit Gibbs phenomena..."
problems.explanation: The memo describes the PQC methods but does not reflect the paper's explicit caveat that training directly on the target interval can produce Gibbs phenomena and that the enlarged interval is used specifically to mitigate this. That limitation is a key methodological condition.

problems.memo_sentence: "The numerical experiments indicate that the proposed PQC-based methods achieve what the authors describe as ‘remarkable accuracy’ and are presented as a competitive quantum alternative for derivatives valuation."
problems.source_evidence: The results section adds important qualifiers: "some outliers appear" due to randomness in initialization; "we need around 5000 shots per coefficient in average, thus implying an order of hundreds of thousand shots"; and "the best performance is obtained with an intermediate scheme (7 × 7 for Method I and 5 × 5 for Method II)."
problems.explanation: The memo emphasizes the positive headline result but underplays the detailed results and caveats in the discussion, especially the need for many shots, the presence of outliers, and the fact that performance depends on intermediate circuit sizes. This is a mild section-bias issue rather than a factual error.
